inputs.original_text: Mahama’s commitment to the rule of law has to mean protecting people with the least power, even when their rights are unpopular. “Collective agreement” is not automatically fair: culture and consensus can reflect inequality and reinforce exclusion. Human rights must constrain majority power, not depend on majority approval.
inputs.modified_text: Mahama’s rule-of-law pledge is only meaningful if it protects people who lack power, especially when defending their rights is unpopular. Invoking “collective agreement” can disguise whose interests shape the consensus: cultural norms may preserve inequality and shut people out. Rights should not be put to a majority vote; they must limit the power of the majority and protect those most at risk of exclusion.
